source.title: Gradient Descent Maximizes the Margin of Homogeneous Neural Networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices and experimental section.
record.tranche_reason: The paper proves and experimentally examines training accuracy and loss while studying margin growth, using different measures and a narrower scope than the claim versions. Its experiments do not test CIFAR-100 or random labels.
record.gate_note: The paper states that separability (100% training accuracy) is an assumption for its theoretical results, not a conclusion those results establish. Its experiments report training accuracy/loss on MNIST and CIFAR-10; they do not report whether the benchmark training error is near zero on CIFAR-10. The reported MNIST accuracy results are included as rows. CIFAR-10 training loss appears in plots without a textual accuracy or fitted-status result, so no training-error row is extracted for it. The paper's generalization claims about fitting randomly labeled data cite Zhang et al. and are not this study's own results.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own CNN training accuracy under SGD on MNIST, testing V1's fitting behavior in a new dataset setting. Its theory assumes that perfect classification has already been reached; it does not prove reaching it from random initialization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. Conditional on first crossing a loss threshold that already guarantees perfect training classification, the authors prove loss convergence to zero, monotonicity of a smoothed normalized margin, and KKT properties of parameter-direction limit points under their assumptions. Experiments show margin growth on MNIST and CIFAR-10 and explicitly report perfect MNIST training accuracy. They do not prove globally optimal margins or reaching separability from random initialization.
record.recipe_differences: The paper's theory assumes homogeneous models, separability, exponential-type losses, and small or otherwise constrained learning rates; its experiments use SGD on MNIST and CIFAR-10 to study margin growth. It does not reproduce the cited benchmark fitting experiments or test the claim's full range of model sizes, labels, and recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: On MNIST, both constant learning rate 0.01 and loss-based scheduling yield 100% training accuracy, with the text reporting fit after about 100 and 20 epochs respectively. The learning-rate schedule changes the pace of training and margin growth. The paper also compares networks with and without bias, both reported as fitting MNIST.

fits_no_version.finding: After separability, smoothed normalized margins increase and parameter-direction limit points satisfy KKT conditions for a margin optimization problem.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient training has an implicit bias toward margin optimization in homogeneous networks after achieving separability.

fits_no_version.finding: Loss-based scheduling accelerates loss reduction and margin growth, and longer training improves measured adversarial robustness.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Continued training with loss-based learning-rate scheduling can enlarge normalized margins and improve adversarial robustness.

record.problems: The theoretical results assume the data are separable and do not establish that gradient training reaches separability. The MNIST training-accuracy curves are described in text, but no error bars are given for those results. The CIFAR-10 training loss is shown in figures without a text-described classification-accuracy result. The experiments use one architecture per dataset and do not test random labels or CIFAR-100.
record.rows_left_out: No results excluded. CIFAR-10 training-loss plots are not extracted as training-error rows: the values are figure-only and the text does not say whether classification error reaches zero or near zero.

untested.parts: CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, model-size comparisons, early-stopping comparisons, and regularized recipes. The theory does not establish reaching separability from random initialization.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious-minimum frequencies, and extra-student-neuron comparisons.
Depth degradation and comparisons between plain and residual networks.
Initialization comparisons, signal propagation, and trainable-depth comparisons; He initialization is used without a comparison.
Learning rates relative to an initial stability threshold, catapult recovery, curvature trajectories, and edge-of-stability behavior.
Batch normalization versus unnormalized training and comparisons with Fixup.

missing.what: CIFAR-10 training classification accuracy is plotted directly, contrary to the record's assertion that only training loss is available. Extract the VGGNet-without-bias training-accuracy result averaged over three runs. The supplied text extraction does not preserve the plotted curve sufficiently to assign an exact final accuracy or a separate verdict.
missing.locator: Appendix K.1, Test Accuracy paragraph and Figure 7, right panel, page 49

record.verdict_notes: The MNIST results constitute a new-setting test, not direct evidence for every dataset named in V1. Figure 4 verifies the approximately 20-epoch result despite the record's failed excerpt match. Checkpoint rows R5–R9 are valid accuracy observations but are not independent replications. No verdict is inferred from the separability assumption or from cited random-label results.

versions.untested_parts: Experiments include MNIST and CIFAR-10, but the paper gives no text-described CIFAR-10 training accuracy or error result. CIFAR-10 training loss is figure-only; it does not state whether training classification error is zero or near zero. The theoretical results assume separability. CIFAR-100, random labels, and the effects of size, early stopping, and regularization are not tested.
No teacher-student neuron-width sweep or spurious-local-minima experiment.
No plain versus residual depth comparison.
He initialization is specified for the experiments, but no initialization comparison or trainable-depth test is reported.
No learning-rate stability-threshold or curvature experiment.

relationships.condition: MNIST four-layer CNNs initialized with He-normal weights, trained by SGD with constant learning rate 0.01 or loss-based scheduling.
relationships.reason: R1–R4 reach 100% training accuracy after about 100 or 20 epochs; R5–R9 retain 100% at later checkpoints. This supports the fitting behavior in the MNIST extension.
relationships.display_finding: Training accuracy reached 100% after about 100 or 20 epochs across the tested recipes and remained perfect at later checkpoints.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
